title: Talking Is Teaching bus posters and donations
summary: The Commission on Children and Youth reviewed bus posters needing about 70 copies, but a speaker said its budget could not cover printing, and whether it may ask for donations was referred for legal advice. In December a speaker cautioned against seeking donations for one organization, and the commission voted on the posters.

timeline.text: A speaker cautioned commissioners against asking for donations for one particular organization.
A commissioner said Maui Family Support Services can take in donations set aside for printing the posters.
The lawyer recommended the department send a request for legal services on whether the commission may ask for donations.
Whether the commission may ask for donations is still being researched.
The lawyer confirmed the poster printing is exempt from the procurement code (purchasing rules).
One speaker said the commission's budget could not cover even the printing.
The chair said $20 per poster was only a guess.
The chair said about 70 posters would be needed.
The chair asked for the poster samples by email so they can be sent to commissioners to review and vote on.
The presenter showed sample posters meant for display on buses.
The commission moved its Talking Is Teaching poster item up because the presenter had to leave early.
